root_cause: When ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() was made failable (returning negative AVERROR codes) as part of a broader refactor to bound Exp-Golomb decoding, the caller in palette_subblock_data() was updated to check the new error condition, but the validation check ('if (coeff < 0) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;') was placed after the arithmetic expression that uses 'coeff' in a multiplication, rather than before it. This ordering mistake allowed the invalid/error sentinel value to participate in signed multiplication, causing overflow.
findings: In palette_subblock_data() (libavcodec/vvc/ctu.c), when decoding an escape-coded palette sample, ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() is called and can return a negative AVERROR value (e.g. AVERROR_INVALIDDATA) on malformed/corrupt bitstreams.
